description: core §4.2, a late joiner's seed over snapshots: the merge of a GET's snapshots and per-key replies with its subscription's samples, the omission rule, asof and pages. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked by a second, never blessed. Every key here is an owner's state key, and every sample carries an in-band stamp, `{width, run, seq}` as `inband.json` writes it, so a consumer's merge and a tool's agree on every case. `collections`: what the reader's contract gives it, each `{coll, template, snapshot_key}`: the collection's index, its template, and its snapshot key (§4.2); a reader without the contract has none. A case may give instead `revisions`, each revision of the interface the reader holds by its fingerprint, with its collections, and `descriptor`, the fingerprint the owner's descriptor names (§3.3): the reader maps a snapshot's coll by that revision's collections alone. `view`: what the reader holds when it asks the GET, each `{key, sample, stamp, record}`, `sample` `put` or `delete`, `record` a put's record in hex. `arrivals`: in order, everything after it asks the GET, each `via` `get` (one of the GET's replies) or `subscription` (a live sample), on `key`: a sample `{sample, stamp, record}` (a per-key resource's reply or `reply_del`, or a live put or delete), or a snapshot's page, `page` as `snapshot/bodies.json` reads one, with its bytes in `hex`. The merge keeps the newer by in-band stamp: within one run, one width and one value, a higher seq; another run is unordered and kept, the later arrival; an equal stamp is one mutation, kept once. A page's entries merge as it arrives, each on its member's key: the page's key, then `/` and the id, the key itself for the empty id. A live entry is a put, a tombstone a delete, each stamped with its own run or the header's, and its seq. One snapshot's pages share their key, tag, run width, run, asof, time and coll. It is complete once it holds each index from 0 to a page whose more bit is 0. Then, on a key K that is the snapshot key or a member's key of the collection with that coll, the omission rule drops each member of the collection at K or under it that the reader holds and the snapshot lists neither live nor as a tombstone, unless held under the snapshot's run with a seq above asof, or under another run and heard after the GET was asked: every arrival was, no view entry was, and a held value heard again by an arrival with its stamp, kept once, then was. A member matches its template under the snapshot key, each parameter one chunk. A page heard on a subscription is neither merged nor counted. `expect.view`: what the reader holds after the last arrival, sorted by key bytes. `expect.snapshots`: each snapshot heard by the GET, in order of its first page, with its key, coll, run, asof, the page indices held, whether it is complete, and the keys its omission rule dropped, sorted.

cases.note: a collection read, one page, into an empty view: each entry is its member's put or delete, on the snapshot key plus its id
entries merge by in-band stamp: a held older value is replaced, a held equal one is the same mutation, kept once
a live put newer than the entry, heard before the page, stands: the entry is older and refused
a tombstone merges as a delete with its stamp: the held put of b is older
a tombstone for a member the view does not hold: held as a deletion
a live delete heard during the GET, newer than the entry, stands
the omission rule: a held member the complete snapshot lists neither live nor as a tombstone has no value, and is dropped
a delete beyond the window: the owner's tombstone is gone, and the snapshot's omission drops the held put
a held deletion the snapshot omits is dropped too: the member holds nothing
an empty snapshot, complete, is the owner's word: every held member of the collection is dropped
the guard, run R: a live put under the snapshot's run with a seq above asof, heard during the GET, is kept
the guard is strict: under the snapshot's run, a seq equal to asof is no newer, and is dropped
by the rule, a live put under the snapshot's run at or below asof is dropped, whenever it arrived
the guard, another run: a value under another run that arrived after the GET was asked is kept
a value under another run held from before the GET is dropped: an earlier instance's member the new run no longer holds
one value at two widths is two runs: a held 32-bit run 5 is not the snapshot's 16-bit run 5, and arrived before the GET
a live sample after completion merges as usual: a put of the omitted member under the snapshot's run is kept
a key under the snapshot key that is no member of the template is not the collection's: never omitted
three pages in order: each page's entries merge as it arrives, and the omission applies once the last has
pages out of order: complete when page 0 arrives last; a live put between pages merges as it comes
a page lost: pages 0 and 2 of 3, incomplete; the entries that arrived merge, and nothing is omitted
only the last page, as `Latest` would keep it: incomplete, nothing omitted
a page twice: one mutation per stamp, and the snapshot complete at its last page
pages of one asof and two times are two snapshots: neither is complete
pages of two asofs are two snapshots: neither is complete
an entry's own run: a member last written under the instance's earlier run keeps it, and merges under it
two instances answer one GET under two runs: each complete snapshot's omission spares the other run's members that arrived after the GET
the same mutation heard again after the GET counts as heard then: a held value of another run, re-heard live, is spared
the same two answers in the other order: the seed holds the same members
a member read: a snapshot of one member on its own key, empty id; it answers for that member alone
a member read of a key the owner holds no member at: one page with no entry on that key, the owner's word; the held member there is dropped, and no other
the same, a value of the member under the snapshot's run with a seq above asof, heard during the GET: kept
a member read of a deleted member: its own key, one tombstone
a template with no parameter is its own snapshot key: the one entry, empty id, is the member, and the collection whole
an empty snapshot of a template with no parameter drops its one held member
two collections share a snapshot key, told apart by coll: `a/{x}`'s snapshot omits nothing of `a`
and `a`'s, empty, drops `a` alone
a reader without the contract: the entries merge on their keys, and no omission applies, since coll maps to no template

the revision the owner's descriptor names maps coll: it names modem.v3 3.3, and the reader holds 3.2 too. By 3.3, coll 11 is `sdu/endpoint/{endpoint}`, whose snapshot key the page rides, so the complete snapshot's omission drops peer-b; 3.2 declares 7 states and has no collection 11
the same reader, the owner's descriptor naming 3.2: coll 4 is `sdu/endpoint/{endpoint}` by 3.2, and peer-b is dropped; by 3.3 it would be `packed/identity`, a collection of another snapshot key

the descriptor names 3.3, and a page on the endpoints' snapshot key says coll 4, 3.2's index for them: by 3.3, 4 is `packed/identity`, whose snapshot key is not the reply's, so the reader applies no omission rule. The entries merge on their keys, and peer-b stays
a snapshot heard on a subscription is no owner's answer: neither merged nor counted toward a complete snapshot
a snapshot heard on a subscription alone changes nothing
a per-key resource's replies merge by stamp, a reply_del as a deletion; a held key no reply answers stays: silence is no verdict
per-key replies and a snapshot in one GET: each merges on its key, and the snapshot's omission reaches its own collection alone
